title: Blood debt must be paid in blood
next_chapter_hook: In the instant that Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul locked its gaze upon Chen Ji, a killing intent never before sensed swept forth from the depths of the Tianqing Sect—the aura of the former Sect Master, Ling Yuan.

text.content: The clamor beneath the Arena Platform seemed separated by a heavy curtain. Chen Ji stood in the shadows, the Jade Slip in his sleeve already tightly gripped. The surrounding disciples whispered among themselves, discussing the omens of Mo Xiansheng's emergence from seclusion, yet none sensed his heart pounding like war drums. 'As the crowd buzzed, a sharp sword light swept across the sky—that was the aura of Mo Xiansheng emerging!' The previous chapter's ending thundered in his mind. The remnant soul guardian actually intended to personally watch his next match? Chen Ji's lips curved slightly, the smile chilling. Mo Xiansheng, are you protecting me or watching over me? His gaze swept the surroundings—toward the Xuanwu Sect, Han Lie was conversing quietly with several elders, his occasional glances carrying undisguised contempt.

dialogue.content: Oh, isn't this the 'trash senior brother' of our Tianqing Sect?
What, still not discouraged after I thrashed you last time?

text.content: Han Lie deliberately raised his voice, drawing the attention of surrounding disciples. His tone dripped with undisguised mockery, as if Chen Ji was already his defeated opponent. In truth, during the Sect Competition three months prior, Chen Ji had indeed lost to him—of course, that was a meticulously calculated defeat. 'A废物 should have废物觉悟,' Han Lie said, stepping closer and lowering his voice. 'Don't think I don't know your little schemes. You think climbing into Su Qingyao's good graces will let you turn your life around? Dream on!' Chen Ji remained silent. He merely raised his head, fixing Han Lie with a gaze近乎怜悯, as if Han Lie were the one being examined, not him.

Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm. He slightly bowed, his posture impeccably respectful, yet the corner of his mouth curved upward almost imperceptibly. '废物确实该有废物的觉悟—so I will keep losing until shixiong finds it boring.' His words were light and carefree, leading everyone present to believe he was showing weakness. Han Lie's expression shifted slightly. He felt something was off about those words but couldn't pinpoint what. Chen Ji had already turned to leave, his figure desolate and forlorn. Only he himself knew his fist in his sleeve was clenched so tightly his knuckles had turned white. Father... Tianji Record... Chen Xuan... These names branded his heart like burning irons.

Returning to a remote corner of the Servants' Quarters, Chen Ji confirmed no one was around before taking the Jade Slip from his sleeve. The slip's surface was simple and unadorned, with mottled marks of time upon it. His fingers gently traced those patterns, stirring an indescribable bitterness in his heart. This Jade Slip was what he discovered last night in the ruins of his father's old residence—that mansion his father once lived in had burned down fifteen years ago, now only broken walls and scorched remnants remained. Had the Tianji Record not vibrated on its own last night, pointing him in that direction, he might never have discovered this hidden relic.

The moment the restriction loosened, a hoarse yet majestic voice suddenly echoed in Chen Ji's mind. That voice carried urgency, benevolence, and heavy worry. Chen Ji shuddered throughout—this was his father's voice! Even after fifteen years, that voice remained so familiar, as if his father had never left. 'Ji'er,' the voice continued, 'if you can hear this message, it means you have become the new master of the Tianji Record. But Father must warn you—the Eye of Heavenly Secrets is not as simple as you imagine. Every prophetic seer throughout history has been its chess piece. Your grandfather was, and so was I.' Chen Ji's hands trembled slightly, his pupils constricting sharply. The Eye of Heavenly Secrets? Grandfather? Father? These three words exploded in his mind like thunder.

dialogue.content: The Tianji Record is its eye planted in the world, and every user will walk toward destruction in the inevitable flow of fate. Father exhausted his entire life trying to escape this predetermined trajectory, yet ultimately...

text.content: The voice paused slightly here, as if suppressing some intense emotion. A moment later, the voice returned, carrying resolve and unwillingness: 'Ji'er, the thing Father regrets most is involving you in this calamity. But since you have seen this message, Father only asks one thing from you—do not repeat the same mistakes. The more you use the Tianji Record, the more severe the backlash becomes. Each time you use it, you draw one step closer to 'that outcome'.' Chen Ji's breathing grew rapid. He thought of every time he used the Tianji Record these past days—every future he foresaw, every Heavenly Fate value he consumed. So all of this had been under the gaze of that so-called 'Eye of Heavenly Secrets'? 'Protect Nian'er well,' the voice ended, carrying infinite tenderness, 'she is the key to everything... But Father ran out of time to tell you more. There is a second layer of sealing within this Jade Slip. Only when you break through Foundation Building and enter the Golden Core realm can you unlock it. Remember, remember!'

The voice cut off abruptly, the residual spiritual energy within the Jade Slip slowly dissipating. Chen Ji stood frozen in place, his fingers gripping the Jade Slip so tightly his knuckles were white. Countless thoughts churned in his mind. His father's words were like sharp knives, brutally piercing his heart. The Eye of Heavenly Secrets. Chess game. Destruction. These words intertwined, weaving an airtight web, and he himself seemed to have been caught within it from the moment of birth. 'Father...' Chen Ji murmured, his voice hoarse and barely recognizable. For fifteen years, he had always believed his father died in an accident, killed by someone from the Demonic Path. His years of endurance, pretense, and scheming were all for the day when he could find the murderer and avenge the blood debt. But now he understood—his father did not die at another's hands, but at the hands of the so-called 'Eye of Heavenly Secrets'.

Rage surged in Chen Ji's chest like magma, almost breaking through the dam of reason. He wanted to roar, to vent, to tear that so-called 'Eye of Heavenly Secrets' to shreds. But just then, his father's final words echoed in his mind once more—'do not repeat the same mistakes.' Chen Ji sharply closed his eyes, taking a deep breath. He had endured in the Servants' Quarters for fifteen long years, all for the day when he could avenge the blood debt. But if he didn't even know who the enemy was, if that enemy was a terrifying existence above the heavens themselves... what chance did he have to oppose it? 'I understand.' Chen Ji opened his eyes, the fire in his gaze gradually calming, replaced by a chilling composure. 'Eye of Heavenly Secrets... I don't care what you are. Someday, I will personally drag you down from that lofty perch.'

A cold voice suddenly came from behind. Chen Ji's pupils constricted as he whirled around, finding a graceful figure had somehow appeared by the window. The Demonic Path Saintess Ye Qing wore a black dress, her features exquisite as a painting, her lips curved in a meaningful smile. 'I thought you were the kind of person who only knew how to act weak and hide your tail between your legs. I didn't expect...' She walked closer slowly, her gaze falling on the Jade Slip in Chen Ji's hand, a glint of something strange flickering in her eyes. 'That you, Chen Ji, also have such a ferocious side.' Chen Ji's expression instantly returned to that dull, timid appearance, as if the earlier coldness had merely been an illusion. 'What brings Miss Ye to this rundown place?' His voice carried several parts of flattery, several parts of panic, the perfect portrayal of a coward who had been scared out of his wits.

dialogue.content: Ye Qing's smile faded, replaced by a grave expression. 'The aura of the Tianji Record, I can sense it from a hundred miles away. Your emotional fluctuation just now was too intense—you almost exposed this thing's existence.' Chen Ji's heart tightened. He had indeed been careless—when he learned the truth about his father, his emotions nearly spiraled out of control. Had he let that anger explode outward, the aura of the Tianji Record would certainly have leaked. 'Thank you for the reminder.' He said quietly, his posture still deferential. Ye Qing shook her head, her gaze carrying a measuring quality. 'You and I are cooperating now—if you get exposed, it does me no good either. However...' Her voice dropped lower. 'You mentioned 'Eye of Heavenly Secrets' just now. Where did you learn this name?'

choice.prompt: Ye Qing seemed especially sensitive to the name 'Eye of Heavenly Secrets,' and Chen Ji needed to decide how to respond.

text.content: "Your father..." Ye Qing raised her head, and Chen Ji noticed a more complex emotion in her gaze. "So this is how Chen Xuan died. No wonder the Holy Sect has been searching for the inheritor of the Tianji Record... So they always knew everything." Her voice was extremely low, carrying a咬牙切齿 hatred. "Chen Ji, the matter of the Heavenly Eye is far more serious than you imagine. Your father wasn't the only one targeted by it—I am too."

dialogue.content: Ye Qing's gaze slightly constricted, but the smile at the corner of her lips deepened. "Ancient books?" She laughed lightly, her voice clear as silver bells. "Chen Ji, do you take me for a three-year-old?"

text.content: Chen Ji's heart tightened, but his expression still maintained one of fear. Ye Qing didn't continue pressing, merely looking deeply at him. "Fine, if you won't speak, I won't force you. But I can tell you one thing—the Heavenly Eye has countless connections to my Holy Sect. The reason I initially cooperated with you was because I sensed that familiar aura on you." Her voice dropped lower. "We are both chess pieces, Chen Ji. The only difference is, whoever realizes this first may have a chance to jump off the chessboard."

dialogue.content: Ye Qing clearly hadn't expected Chen Ji to suddenly counter with a question. Her pupils slightly contracted. In those ink-black eyes, a flash of surprise appeared, immediately replaced by a hint of playfulness.

text.content: "Interesting." Ye Qing lightly clapped her hands, her smile gaining a fraction more sincerity. "I thought you were just a spineless waste,没想到也有这样锋芒毕露的时候." She收起笑意,声音低沉,"罢了,看在你今日让我看到有趣一面的份上,我便告诉你——圣宗的圣女,每一任都要在天道之眼下立下血誓。我是第三个, 而在我之前的两位师姐,都已经'死'了。"她特意在"死"字上加重了语气,其中含义不言自明。"

Chen Ji沉默片刻,将玉简收入袖中。无论他选择哪种方式应对,夜清透露的信息都让他心头更加沉重。圣宗、血誓、天道之眼……这些线索正在逐渐串联成一张巨大的网,而他和夜清,都不过是这张网上的两只困兽。"比赛快开始了。"夜清率先打破沉默,目光意味深长地看了陈机一眼,"与韩烈一战,你有几成把握?"陈机没有回答,只是缓缓抬起头,望向远处的比武场方向。他的目光平静得可怕,平静得让人看不出任何情绪。"三成。"他淡淡说道,"但已经足够了。"

Ye Qing was slightly stunned, then laughed lightly. "Three chances?" She shook her head. "You are quite frank. However..." Her gaze lingered on Chen Ji's face for a moment, as if reassessing this "waste." "If you truly had a hundred percent guarantee, it probably wouldn't be just three chances. How much calculation is hidden in your three chances?" Chen Ji didn't answer, only turning to walk toward the door. His figure was bleak and lonely, yet also revealing an inexplicable resolve. "Chen Ji." Ye Qing's voice came from behind, carrying a complex meaning. "Your father was right. The more you use the Tianji Record, the heavier the backlash. You... take it easy." Chen Ji's footsteps paused slightly, then he continued forward, his voice drifting back, calm and firm: "Thank you for the reminder. But there are some things, even knowing they are a dead end, that must be walked."

The Arena was already filled with disciples, their discussions rising and falling. When Chen Ji appeared at the entrance, countless gazes shot over—curiosity, disdain, and undisguised mockery. "That waste actually dares to come?" "I heard Senior Han will finish him within ten moves this time." "Hmph, even moves are unnecessary, one finger would be enough." Chen Ji ignored them all, walking slowly toward the Arena Platform. His gaze swept across the crowd, finally landing on the high platform—Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul phantom was quietly suspended there, those profound eyes seeming to see through all pretense, directly looking into Chen Ji's heart. Chen Ji met that gaze for an instant, then looked away. He continued forward, his steps steady and resolute. His father's last words still echoed in his ears, the shadow of the Heavenly Eye loomed overhead, yet his face showed not a trace of panic or fear.

Across the Arena Platform, Han Lie stood proudly. Clad in Xuanwu Sect's distinctive black battle armor, his aura surged like a storm. His Nascent Soul stage cultivation was released without reservation, pressing down on the lower-level disciples around him until they could barely breathe. "Waste, you actually dare to come?" Han Lie sneered, his eyes full of contempt. Chen Ji slowly stepped onto the Arena Platform, stopping three zhang away from Han Lie. He raised his head, looking at Han Lie with an almost hollow gaze, yet the corner of his lips slowly curved into a barely perceptible arc. That arc made Han Lie inexplicably feel a chill, as if some dangerous aura was approaching. "Senior Han," Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm, "please advise." As his words fell, the Arena Platform's restrictions roared to life, enveloping the two of them. The Law Enforcement Elder's voice rang across the entire grounds—"Combat begins!"

text.content: In an instant, Chen Ji's vision turned pitch black. Immediately, countless lights and shadows flickered past his eyes like flowing water—those were the various possibilities within the next three hours. He saw Han Lie's first move—the Xuanwu Sky-Breaking Fist, aimed directly at his chest's vital point; he also saw the second move, the third move... every trajectory, every flaw, presented clearly before his eyes. When he opened his eyes, a faint smile had already curved his lips. Han Lie's fist was charging toward his chest, carrying the violent power of the Golden Core stage, enough to severely injure any Foundation Building cultivator. But in Chen Ji's eyes, that fist moved as slowly as a snail crawling, its openings as wide as a city gate left ajar.

"Get lost!" Han Lie roared, his fist carrying surging spiritual energy toward Chen Ji. The pressure of the Golden Core stage bore down like a mountain, compressing the surrounding air until it emitted sharp shrieks. "Brother Han is mighty!" "Kill that废物with one punch!" Cheering came from below the stage, as if victory was already decided. Just as the fist was about to touch Chen Ji's chest, he moved. No superfluous movements—merely a sidestep, a跨步, a punch—the motion simple to the point of being crude, yet the point of impact impossibly precise. His fist grazed the inner side of Han Lie's arm and struck the vital point of his Shoulder Well Acupuncture. Han Lie's entire arm went numb and weak, his fist's momentum instantly collapsed. "Wha... what?!" Han Lie's pupils contracted sharply, his face full of disbelief.

text.content: Chen Ji did not dodge. He merely slightly shifted his body, trying to evade Han Lie's attack. But the gap between Golden Core and Foundation Building—how could technique compensate? Han Lie's fist grazed his shoulder, and a violent spiritual energy instantly invaded his meridians, sending his entire body flying. "Bang!" Chen Ji heavily crashed at the edge of theArena Platform, a mouthful of blood spurting out. "废物就是废物。" Han Lie coldly smiled, his gaze full of contempt, "I haven't even used one-tenth of my strength, and you already can't hold on? How boring." Laughter erupted below the stage; someone even started heckling for Han Lie to quickly end the fight. Chen Ji climbed up from the ground, wiped the blood from his lips, his eyes lowered, his posture wretched to the extreme. But beneath those drooping eyelids, a pair of pupils was terrifyingly calm. Mo Xiansheng... Chen Ji silently thought that name in his heart. Are you watching me? Then let you see clearly, just how much of a "废物" this "废物" truly is.

text.content: Just as Han Lie pressed forward with confidence, Chen Ji's wrist suddenly flipped. A talisman radiating cold light appeared in his palm; intricate patterns were drawn upon it, emanating a chilling pressure that made hearts race. "This is..." Han Lie's expression drastically changed, he instinctively sensed danger, "A talisman?!" Chen Ji gave him no time to react. Injecting spiritual energy into the talisman, that cold light instantly surged, transforming into a fierce sword light that headed directly for Han Lie's face. "Stop!" Several elders on the high platform rose simultaneously. But before their voices even finished echoing, that sword light had already slashed Han Lie's shoulder, sending his entire body flying. Blood splattered; Han Lie let out a miserable shriek. The battle armor on his shoulder had been hacked open by a crack.

Silence descended upon theArena. Everyone froze, staring in disbelief at the scene before them. That废物everyone had mocked actually wounded Xuanwu Sect's number one genius? Han Lie clutched his shoulder, his face full of disbelief. Blood seeped through his fingers, dyeing his palm red. "How... how could you..." His voice trembled, eyes filled with terror and fury. Chen Ji slowly retracted the talisman, his face pale as paper. That talisman was one of the trump cards his father left, called the "Truth-Breaking Talisman," capable of breaking through any defense below the Golden Core stage. But it could only be used once; now it had become a scrap of paper. "You've bested me." Chen Ji's voice was flat, as if this were merely an ordinary sparring match. However, the area below the stage exploded into chaos—clamoring voices, exclamations one after another. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul phantom floated above the high platform, those deep eyes firmly fixed on Chen Ji, seemingly contemplating something.

On the Arena Platform, Chen Ji and Han Lie stood facing each other. The air was filled with the smell of blood and tense gunpowder. Han Lie's shoulder was still bleeding; those eyes were nearly shooting flames. "Chen Ji!" He gnashed his teeth and roared, "You dare injure me?!" Chen Ji gave no answer, merely standing there quietly, his gaze terrifyingly calm. The referee elders looked at each other in uncertainty, not knowing how to adjudicate. This competition had clearly deviated from normal tracks, but according to rules, as long as neither party conceded, the match must continue. "Chen Ji!" Han Lie roared again, spiritual energy around him surged violently; the blood at his wound actually clotted in an instant. His momentum climbed again to a terrifying height. "I will make you pay the price!"

At this moment, a sharp aura suddenly swept down from the high platform. That aura was cold and majestic, like a basin of cold water poured on a boiling pot of oil, instantly suppressing the tense, sword-drawn atmosphere on the Arena Platform. "Enough." Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul phantom slowly spoke. Though his voice was soft, it carried undeniable authority. "This battle... is a draw." At these words, the entire venue erupted. "A draw? How could that废物possibly draw with Brother Han?" "What does Elder Mo mean?" "Could it be... could Elder Mo be favoring that废物?" Exclamations rose one after another. Countless gazes turned toward the high platform. Han Lie's expression was even more unsightly. "Elder Mo! By what right do you rule a draw? I haven't lost yet!" Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul phantom slightly turned toward him. Those deep eyes held no emotion whatsoever, yet Han Lie's voice stopped mid-sentence. "Your shoulder wound cannot heal within three days." Mo Xiansheng said lightly. "Does that count as your loss, or his?"

dialogue.content: Han Lie still wanted to argue, but was pulled back by an arriving Xuanwu Sect elder. "Silence!" The elder低声呵斥, cold sweat beading on his forehead. "Elder Mo is the sect's Grand Elder. Do you dare question his judgment?" Only then did Han Lie realize his indiscretion. His face flushed red, yet he had no choice but to swallow this anger. He fiercely glared at Chen Ji, his gaze full of venom, "Chen Ji, you remember this!" Chen Ji remained expressionless, merely slightly bowing in the direction of Elder Mo. "Thank you, Elder Mo, for presiding over fairness." His voice was respectful and humble, yet deep in his heart, waves of turbulence surged. Mo Xiansheng... what are you trying to do? Are you protecting me, or testing me? Does Father's last words about "not repeating the same mistakes" include you?

text.content: After the competition, Chen Ji dragged his exhausted body back to the Servants' Quarters. He closed the door and set up a simple soundproof barrier before leaning against the wall and letting out a long breath. Too much had happened today. The information revealed in Father's testament, Han Lie's provocation, Elder Mo's intervention... each matter was enough to affect his subsequent plans. More importantly, he had to break through his cultivation level as soon as possible to unseal the second layer within the Jade Slip. Father said there was "the key to everything" inside—what on earth was it? Chen Nian... Chen Ji closed his eyes; the name of his sister, missing for many years, surfaced in his mind. Father said she was "the key to everything," but where is she now? Being taken by the Holy Sect as a "Heavenly Fate Lock-Key"—this information Ye Qing had inadvertently revealed, now echoed endlessly in Chen Ji's mind. Holy Sect... Ye Qing... the Eye of Heaven's Mandate... these clues were gradually connecting into a terrifying truth.

Just as Chen Ji fell into contemplation, a slight sound came from outside the window. He instantly became alert; his wrist flipped, and a defensive talisman was already charged and ready. "It's me." A cold voice came from outside the window. Chen Ji slightly startled, then put the talisman away. The window was gently pushed open; a figure vaulted in. It was Su Qingyao. She still had that icy demeanor, but when she saw Chen Ji's pale complexion and the bloodstains on his collar, her brow still slightly furrowed. "You're injured?" Her tone was still cold, yet in those eyes flashed a hint of unconceivable concern. Chen Ji quickly switched to his cowardly expression. "Senior Sister Su, why are you here?" Su Qingyao gave no answer; she merely took out a jade bottle from her sleeve and tossed it to Chen Ji. "Healing elixir. Don't delay your cultivation." With that, she turned to leave.

Su Qingyao's footsteps slightly paused, but she didn't look back. "Today's competition..." Her voice lowered, carrying a hint of probing, "That talisman you used at the end—where did it come from?" Chen Ji's heart tightened, but his expression remained calm. "It was a relic left by my father. I've always kept it close. Only today, in desperation, did I have to use it." Su Qingyao was silent for a moment, seemingly judging the truth of his words. "Your father..." Her voice softened slightly. "I've heard sect elders mention him. Chen Xuan, once also a genius disciple of Tianqing Sect, later disappeared for unknown reasons. Some say he defected; others say he died at the hands of the Demonic Path..." She finally turned around, her gaze burning as she stared at Chen Ji. "What is the truth?"

dialogue.content: Chen Ji lowered his eyes, his voice carrying a hint of sorrow, 'Father offended someone from the Demonic Path back then and was pursued by enemies. I was young at the time, only remembering a great fire... When the sect's people rescued me, Father had already disappeared without a trace.'

text.content: Su Qingyao watched him quietly, her gaze deep and sharp, as if she could see through all pretense. After a long while, she sighed softly, 'You don't have to hide so much from me.' Her voice carried a trace of disappointment, 'I know you have secrets, and I know you're not as simple as you appear. But since you're unwilling to speak, I won't force you.' She walked toward the window, and before leaving, she glanced at Chen Ji one final time, 'Chen Ji, I don't know what you're planning, but there's something I must warn you about - Former Sect Master Ling Yuan has been paying close attention to you lately. You should be more careful.' With that, she flipped out the window and vanished into the night. Chen Ji stood in place, gazing at the direction where Su Qingyao disappeared, his expression growing deep and unfathomable. Ling Yuan... that name again. Although his father's dying words hadn't mentioned him, Su Qingyao's warning made him heighten his vigilance. What was this scheming sect master really planning?

dialogue.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, as if making a difficult decision. Finally, he lifted his head, his voice extremely low, 'Senior Sister Su, have you ever heard of... the Eye of Heavenly Way?' Su Qingyao's body visibly trembled. 'The Eye of Heavenly Way?' Her voice tightened slightly, 'Where did you hear this name?'

text.content: Chen Ji shook his head, 'I don't know what it is. But among Father's legacy, it mentions... his death was related to this 'Eye of Heavenly Way'.' Su Qingyao's expression turned grave. She remained silent for a long time before slowly speaking, 'Chen Ji, this matter... is far more complicated than I imagined.' Her gaze sharpened, 'I have only seen fragments of the name 'Eye of Heavenly Way' in extremely secret records. It is said to be a mysterious organization from ancient times, specializing in manipulating the fate of the world. If your father was really targeted by them...' She didn't continue, but the implication was self-evident. Chen Ji watched Su Qingyao's solemn expression and felt a slight relief in his heart. It seemed Su Qingyao knew less than he had imagined; at least she didn't know about the existence of the Tianji Record. In that case, temporarily revealing the existence of the 'Eye of Heavenly Way' shouldn't expose too much.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji closed the doors and windows, setting up multiple sound insulation formations before turning around, his gaze carrying unprecedented solemnity. 'Senior Sister Su, you are the only person I trust in the Tianqing Sect. There are things I shouldn't have told you, but since you've investigated this far...' He paused, taking out the faintly glowing fragment from his chest. 'This is what Father left me - the Tianji Record.'

text.content: Su Qingyao's pupils contracted sharply. As the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, she had naturally heard legends of the Tianji Record - a supreme treasure from ancient times that could predict the future but would also bring terrible backlash. But she had never imagined that this legendary object would be right here, in Chen Ji's hands. 'The Tianji Record...' Her voice trembled slightly, and she reached out to touch it, yet pulled back at the last moment. 'Have you used it?' Chen Ji nodded, 'Each use consumes Heavenly Fate Value. And my Heavenly Fate Value... is running out.' Su Qingyao fell silent. Her gaze lingered on Chen Ji's face for a long time, as if seeing him anew. Finally, she sighed softly, 'No wonder... no wonder you could endure for so long in front of everyone. Chen Ji, how did you survive these fifteen years?' This question made Chen Ji freeze momentarily. He lifted his head, meeting Su Qingyao's complex eyes, and an indescribable warmth rose in his heart. Fifteen years - this was the first person who didn't treat him as worthless.

text.content: After Su Qingyao left, Chen Ji sat alone in the dim room, his mind constantly replaying everything that had happened today. Father's dying words, Han Lie's provocation, Mo Xiansheng's intervention, Su Qingyao's warning... every clue pointed to an increasingly clear truth, yet they intertwined into a suffocating web. 'The Eye of Heavenly Way...' Chen Ji murmured, a determined light flickering in his eyes. He took out the jade slip his father had left him, fingers gently tracing the mottled patterns on its surface. Second level seal... Foundation Building realm... Father said that Nian was the key to everything... Chen Nian, his missing sister for years - where was she now? At the Holy Sect? Chen Ji closed his eyes and took a deep breath. When he opened his eyes again, they had regained their usual calm and depth. 'Wait for me, Nian.' he said quietly, his voice carrying unwavering determination. 'No matter where you are, I will find you. No matter who the culprit is, I will make them pay the price.' Outside the window, the night was as dark as ink, with neither stars nor moonlight. In the distant horizon, something seemed to be stirring restlessly.
